prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.
Recommended: Joining technology lectures at LWF for 'Joining of Lightweight Structures' course.
Basic knowledge of engineering mechanics, materials science and manufacturing technology is recommended for 'Manufacturing of Lightweight Structures' course.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are familiar with the procedures, concepts, and methods of lightweight manufacturing, can apply them, and critically evaluate the results.

Students can reproduce the fundamentals of relevant lightweight materials and list, describe, and evaluate application-appropriate joining processes. Connection technology plays a key role in lightweight construction.
Students can constructively design, characterize, and shape connections and evaluate them regarding economic and technological aspects.
Students are able to analyze, evaluate, and master the interactions of manufacturing with the structure, materials, and use.
Students know the advantages and disadvantages of various manufacturing processes in lightweight construction and are able to implement and evaluate suitable processes for specific problems.

Students are able to apply the acquired knowledge and methods to real-world problems, specifically implementing the concept of optimizing lightweight construction. They successfully resolve the tension between costs, benefits, and availability of materials and manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: Application aspects and property profiles of technical lightweight materials
Joining of high-strength steel sheets, Al, Mg, and fiber composite materials
Joining of materials in material mix
Constructive design and shaping of connections
Economic and technological application aspects for various joining processes
Fundamentals of lightweight structures: design methods, evaluation of lightweight structures, structural characteristics and consequences for manufacturing technology
Lightweight materials: Ultra-high strength steels, light metals (aluminum, magnesium, titanium) and composites
Manufacturing processes for metal-based lightweight structures: press hardening, hot forming of light metals, additive manufacturing processes, etc.
Manufacturing processes for polymer-based lightweight structures: thermoforming, RTM, autoclave processes, resin infusion processes, etc.
Manufacturing processes for hybrid lightweight structures
Selection and evaluation of manufacturing processes
Consideration and analysis of practical examples
assessment_rules: The module completion examination consists of a written exam (180-240 minutes) or an oral exam (45-60 minutes). The examination requires students to explain underlying mechanisms and select and evaluate suitable processes for manufacturing and joining lightweight structures based on exemplary problems. Performance points are awarded upon passing the module completion examination.
